next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election

glance_notes.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Online Voter Registration
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Kentucky's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5, 2026. Online registration must be completed by 4:00 p.m. local time.

glance_notes.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Dates
glance_notes.text: Three Days of No-Excuse Early Voting: Kentucky provides three days of no-excuse in-person absentee voting immediately before Election Day week. For the 2026 General Election, those dates are October 29, October 30 and October 31. Any qualified registered voter may use this option without providing a reason.

glance_notes.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Absentee Voting by Mail
glance_notes.text: Mail-In Absentee Voting Requires Eligibility: Kentucky does not provide unrestricted no-excuse absentee voting by mail. A voter must qualify under one of the reasons established by state law. For the 2026 General Election, the online mail-in absentee request portal is scheduled to be open from September 19 through October 20.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Kentucky residents may register online, by mail or in person. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be a Kentucky resident for at least 28 days before the election, be at least 18 years old by the next General Election, not claim the right to vote outside Kentucky, and not have had voting rights removed by a court because of mental incompetence. A person convicted of a felony must have voting rights restored through an applicable legal process before registering. Kentucky permits 17-year-olds to preregister if they will be 18 by the next General Election; those voters may also vote in the preceding Primary Election.
register.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: The State Board's voter-registration guidance establishes online, mail and in-person registration. The Board's voter-registration-drive guidance at [https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voter-Registration-Drives.aspx](https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voter-Registration-Drives.aspx) directly establishes citizenship, 28-day Kentucky residence, age, felony-rights restoration, mental-competency and single-voting-residence requirements. Kentucky also offers registration through county clerks, driver's-license offices and designated public-assistance and disability-service agencies.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Kentucky voters can verify their voter registration through the state's official GoVoteKY voter portal. Voters should check their record after moving or legally changing their name because those changes require an updated registration. County clerks maintain local voter registration records and can assist with registration questions.
check_registration.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — GoVoteKY
check_registration.internal_note: The State Board voter-registration FAQ at [https://elect.ky.gov/Frequently-Asked-Questions/Pages/Voter-Registration.aspx](https://elect.ky.gov/Frequently-Asked-Questions/Pages/Voter-Registration.aspx) directly instructs voters to verify registration through govote.ky.gov and confirms that registration must be updated after a move or legal name change.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The registration deadline for Kentucky's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5, 2026. Online applications must be completed by 4:00 p.m. local time. Kentucky closes voter registration before each election and does not provide general Election Day voter registration. Once the registration deadline has passed, registration records generally cannot be updated until after the election.
deadlines.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Online Voter Registration
deadlines.internal_note: The live official registration portal specifically states that the November 3, 2026 General Election registration deadline is October 5, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. local time. The State Board homepage independently lists October 5 as the last registration day. The voter-registration FAQ states that after the deadline passes the voter registration rolls are frozen until after the election.

polling_place.label: Find a Voting Location
polling_place.content: Use Kentucky's official GoVoteKY voter portal to find your voting locations. Kentucky counties publish locations for Election Day voting, excused in-person absentee voting and no-excuse in-person absentee voting. Because locations can differ depending on the voting method and county, verify the appropriate location before going to vote.
polling_place.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — GoVoteKY
polling_place.internal_note: The official 2026 absentee portal specifically directs voters to the state's polling-location service for locations covering excused in-person absentee voting, no-excuse in-person absentee voting and Election Day voting. County election officials establish local voting sites.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Kentucky's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 6:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. prevailing local time. A voter who is in line by 6:00 p.m. has the right to vote. Kentucky generally requires voters to establish their identity at the polling place using an accepted form of identification. A voter who cannot satisfy the identification requirement may be eligible to use Kentucky's alternative identification procedure or cast a provisional ballot when applicable.
election_day.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Voter Rights
election_day.internal_note: The State Board directly confirms the right of voters in line by 6:00 p.m. to vote. The official 2026 Kentucky Election Guide at [https://www.sos.ky.gov/Documents/2026%20Kentucky%20Election%20Guide.pdf](https://www.sos.ky.gov/Documents/2026%20Kentucky%20Election%20Guide.pdf) states Election Day hours are 6:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. prevailing time. Kentucky spans Eastern and Central time zones, so prevailing local time is important.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Kentucky polls are open from 6:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. prevailing local time on Election Day. Anyone who is in line to vote by 6:00 p.m. is allowed to remain and vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Kentucky Secretary of State — 2026 Kentucky Election Guide
polling_hours.internal_note: The official 2026 Election Guide directly establishes 6:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. prevailing-time polling hours. The State Board voter-rights page at [https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voter-Rights.aspx](https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voter-Rights.aspx) independently confirms that a voter in line by 6:00 p.m. may vote.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Kentucky provides both excused and no-excuse in-person absentee voting before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, qualified voters with an accepted excuse may vote in person on October 21, 22, 23, 26, 27 and 28. No-excuse in-person absentee voting is available to all qualified registered voters on October 29, 30 and 31. Locations and hours vary by county, so voters should check their county's official voting locations and schedule.
early_voting.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Dates
early_voting.internal_note: The current State Board homepage directly lists October 21-23 and October 26-28 for excused in-person absentee voting and October 29-31 for no-excuse in-person absentee voting. The live 2026 General Election absentee portal at [https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/abrweb](https://vrsws.sos.ky.gov/abrweb) independently confirms all three voting options and dates. Exact daily hours and sites are county-specific.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Kentucky requires voters requesting a mail-in absentee ballot to qualify under a reason established by state law. Eligible categories include certain military and overseas voters, students temporarily living outside their county of residence, certain jailed voters who have not been convicted, voters temporarily residing outside Kentucky, voters absent from their county during all available in-person voting periods, participants in Kentucky's address confidentiality program, and voters unable to appear in person because of age, disability or illness. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the online absentee request portal opens September 19 and closes October 20. Completed mail-in absentee ballots must be received by the county clerk by 6:00 p.m. on Election Day.
absentee_mail.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: The State Board's current absentee page directly lists eight categories eligible to use the online mail-in absentee portal. The State Board homepage establishes the September 19 and October 20 portal dates for the 2026 General Election. The disability-voting page at [https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voters-with-Disabilities.aspx](https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voters-with-Disabilities.aspx) directly confirms the 6:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline. The State Board currently notes that USPS recommends mailing completed ballots no later than October 27, but that recommendation is not the legal deadline.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Kentucky voters casting a ballot in person are generally required to present an accepted form of identification. A driver's license is accepted, and other qualifying photo identification issued by the United States, Kentucky, the U.S. Department of Defense, a college or university, or a local government in Kentucky may also qualify. The identification must contain the voter's name and photograph. Kentucky law also provides an alternative procedure for a voter who cannot obtain qualifying photo identification: the voter may sign an affirmation and present an accepted secondary document, such as a Social Security card, credit or debit card, another identification card containing the voter's name and photograph, or certain documents issued by a government entity showing the voter's name.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID generally required; alternative procedure available
voter_id.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Voter Rights
voter_id.internal_note: Kentucky's current voter-ID framework is established by KRS 117.227 and summarized in official State Board and Secretary of State election materials. The 2026 Kentucky Election Guide at [https://www.sos.ky.gov/Documents/2026%20Kentucky%20Election%20Guide.pdf](https://www.sos.ky.gov/Documents/2026%20Kentucky%20Election%20Guide.pdf) instructs voters to bring photo identification. The State Board voter-rights page confirms that voters without identification may cast a provisional ballot in applicable circumstances. The reader-facing text preserves Kentucky's statutory alternative affirmation process rather than incorrectly describing the law as an absolute photo-ID requirement.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Kentucky provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities. ADA-approved voting machines are available for early in-person absentee voting and Election Day voting. A voter may bring someone to provide assistance or request assistance from election officers, subject to applicable law. Voters with qualifying disabilities may request a mail-in absentee ballot. Kentucky also provides an accessible Disability Absentee Portal for voters whose disability prevents them from marking a paper ballot. The electronic ballot can be marked using a mouse, keyboard or compatible assistive device, then must be printed and returned using the required envelopes. The completed ballot must reach the county clerk by 6:00 p.m. on Election Day.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible machines, assistance and accessible absentee voting
accessible_voting.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: The current State Board disability page directly establishes ADA-approved machines, assistance, ordinary mail-in absentee voting and the Disability Absentee Portal. It states that voters should contact their county clerk to request access to the disability portal and that electronically marked ballots must ultimately be printed and returned physically by 6:00 p.m. Election Day.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Kentucky provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible military members, their qualifying dependents and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use federal military and overseas voting procedures to register and request a ballot, including the Federal Post Card Application. Kentucky also provides electronic delivery of blank ballots to eligible military and overseas voters. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot may be used as a backup by qualifying voters when necessary. Because registration, ballot transmission and return procedures differ from ordinary domestic absentee voting, military and overseas voters should use Kentucky's official military and overseas voter resources for the deadlines and methods that apply to their circumstances.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic ballot delivery and FWAB available
military_overseas.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Kentucky operates specialized UOCAVA procedures under KRS Chapter 117A. Official Kentucky materials confirm that the state's military and overseas voter portal permits electronic voter-registration activity and electronic delivery of blank ballots. This section deliberately avoids applying the October 20 ordinary absentee-request deadline or ordinary domestic ballot-return rules to UOCAVA voters because separate statutory deadlines and procedures apply.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student may register in Kentucky if the student establishes Kentucky residence and otherwise meets the state's voter qualifications. A Kentucky voter who is a student temporarily residing outside the county of the voter's permanent residence is specifically eligible to request a mail-in absentee ballot. Students should register and vote using only one legal voting residence and should update their registration if their legal residence changes.
student_voting.glance_value: Students away from their county may qualify for mail voting
student_voting.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Absentee Voting by Mail
student_voting.internal_note: The State Board's current absentee page explicitly identifies a student who temporarily resides outside the county of residence as eligible for mail-in absentee voting. Kentucky voter-registration requirements are established at [https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voter-Registration-Drives.aspx](https://elect.ky.gov/Voters/Pages/Voter-Registration-Drives.aspx). The section does not imply that attending a Kentucky college automatically establishes Kentucky voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Kentucky voters have the right to review a sample ballot before voting. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's county, precinct and electoral districts, voters should use Kentucky's official GoVoteKY voter resources or their county clerk's election information to obtain the ballot that applies to them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Review your official local sample ballot
sample_ballot.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections — Voter Rights
sample_ballot.internal_note: The State Board's Voter Rights page directly establishes a voter's right to review a sample ballot before voting. Ballot content varies locally, so county clerks and the state voter portal are the appropriate official sources for voter-specific ballot information. Reverify closer to the General Election as finalized sample ballots are published.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Kentucky State Board of Elections, 140 Walnut Street, Frankfort, KY 40601. Phone: 502-573-7100. For voter registration, absentee voting, polling locations and other election questions, voters may also contact their county clerk. The State Board maintains Kentucky's statewide voter registration database and oversees compliance with state and federal election law.
contact.internal_note: The State Board voter-rights page directly provides 502-573-7100 as the State Board contact number. Official State Board resources identify 140 Walnut Street, Frankfort, KY 40601 as the Board's office. County clerk contact information is available through [https://elect.ky.gov/Resources/Pages/default.aspx](https://elect.ky.gov/Resources/Pages/default.aspx). No unverified email address is inserted into reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Kentucky State Board of Elections and GoVoteKY for official statewide election information, voter registration, registration verification, voting locations, absentee-ballot information, election dates and voter resources. Kentucky's 120 county clerks administer many local election functions, including voter registration processing, polling and early-voting locations, absentee ballots and local ballot information.

official_resources.internal_note: Official voter portal: [https://govote.ky.gov/](https://govote.ky.gov/).
